# Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing — LINK-ONLY reference card

- **Source:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing
- **Author:** Maintained by Wikipedia's WikiProject AI Cleanup — human editors cataloguing AI-generated text patterns since 2023
- **License:** CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikipedia text license). Linked here rather than copied to keep this corpus tight.

## What slop it prevents
This is the canonical human-curated catalogue of AI writing tells — inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague attributions, signposting phrases, overused vocabulary, formatting tells, and more — each with real before/after examples from detected AI submissions. Both stop-slop and anti-ai-slop-writing (see INDEX) build their banned lists partly on this page; it is the primary source behind them.

## How we use it
- **Reference behind the review step:** when a dev-room report, release note, or piece of in-game text "smells like AI", check it against this catalogue to name the specific tell instead of vaguely rewriting.
- **Basis for a future Japanese tell list:** the catalogue's categories (not its English word lists) are the template if we later write a みゅけ-specific Japanese anti-slop checklist for staff chatter, quest text, and report prose.
- Also useful as a *detector-side* checklist for reviewing text that arrives from outside (PR descriptions, generated docs) before it enters the project.
